title: Identifiability of Personal Health Data
description: The wearable device continuously captures and processes highly personal sensor telemetry including heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps. This data is inherently identifiable to the specific wearer (EE1) and can be used to create detailed profiles of the user's health status, location patterns, and daily activities.

title: Linkability of Sensor Data Across Time and Contexts
description: The continuous stream of sensor data (GPS, timestamps, activity metrics) can be linked across different time periods and contexts to infer sensitive information about the user's routines, locations, health conditions, and social patterns that may not be apparent from individual data points.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health and Location Data
description: The wearable device may transmit collected sensor telemetry to external systems (cloud services, third-party apps, analytics platforms) without adequate access controls, potentially exposing sensitive health metrics and precise location information to unauthorized parties.

title: Manipulation of Sensor Telemetry Data
description: The sensor data captured by the wearable device could be altered, tampered with, or falsified by malicious actors with access to the device or its communication channels, compromising the integrity of health records and activity tracking.

title: Usurpation of User Identity and Data Access
description: If the wearable device is stolen, lost, or accessed by unauthorized individuals, they could potentially impersonate the user (EE1) or access the user's personal health and location data without proper authentication mechanisms.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations for Health Data
description: The continuous collection and processing of sensitive health data (heart rate, activity metrics) and location information may not comply with applicable privacy regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or other health data protection laws, creating legal and compliance risks.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure from Wearable Device to Companion App
description: The wearable device (P1) explicitly transfers personal data including GPS traces, device IDs, timestamps, and exercise session data to the companion mobile app (P2). This represents an intentional data disclosure across a process boundary. The GPS traces in particular can reveal detailed location patterns and movement history, which may be more sensitive than necessary for basic app functionality.
assumptions: The wearable device is designed to sync all sensor data to the companion app without user consent for each sync operation.
